questions.q: What is the real purpose of an after-action report (AAR)?
options: To turn a lessons learned meeting's findings into a durable, structured record the organization can act on and reference later
To replace the lessons learned meeting entirely
To assign personal blame for the incident
To satisfy a legal requirement with no operational value
questions.explain: A meeting's findings live only in memory unless a written AAR captures them as a durable, actionable record.

questions.q: Which of these is part of a real AAR's root cause section?
options: The actual underlying reason the incident happened, such as a phished credential or unpatched vulnerability — not just the symptom that triggered the alert
A list of every employee who was online that day
The stock price of the company on the day of the incident
A guess at what might happen next year
questions.explain: Root cause goes beyond the triggering symptom to the actual underlying reason the incident occurred.

questions.q: Why does "Improve logging" fail as a real action item?
options: It has no named owner, no deadline, and no specific checkable outcome
Logging can never actually be improved
Action items are not allowed to mention technical systems
It's too short to be understood
questions.explain: A real action item names a specific person or team, a deadline, and a checkable outcome — vague goals don't count.

questions.q: In the business email compromise follow-up example, what specific action item did Priya (SOC lead) take on?
options: Adding a step to the IR playbook requiring MFA status be checked within the first five minutes of any account-compromise incident
Granting read access to the identity provider's MFA-status API
Firing the analyst who missed the alert
Rewriting the entire incident response plan from scratch
questions.explain: Priya's action item was a specific playbook change with a clear, checkable outcome and a one-week deadline.

questions.q: What does a good AAR drive, beyond simply documenting what happened?
options: Real organizational change — budget requests, policy updates, and tooling fixes with owners and deadlines
Nothing; its only purpose is historical record-keeping
A reduction in the number of incidents reported to management
A requirement to repeat the exact same incident annually for testing
questions.explain: A report with specific, owned, dated action items is what turns a documented incident into real organizational change.
